page.layout: One page of running text, set in one block with no marginal notes. Running head at the top centre: "DEDICATORIA." Page number and gathering signature at the foot right.

main_text.p: thodi, lumen ex ⌣Aristotelis nactus est legibus, ut totus jam Christianus orbis divina Methodo dispositas artes satis mirari nequeat. Quis enim ante Petri Rami tempora artes tam breviter, ut nunc sunt, Methodo conscriptas vidit? nonne omnis artium tradendarum via vepribus, dumis, & rubis hirsutis ac densis obsita fuit? Verum enimvero PRINCEPS Illustriss. ut evenire solet, saepe inveterata consuetudo tantum habet ponderis ac roboris, ut etiam veritatem sua corruscatione⌣ aciem oculorum hominum offendentem opprimere posse videatur. Quocirca quum vidissem, quod multi prorsus Petri Rami artes aurea conscriptas Methodo, ob difficultatem, quam praetendebat, pro nihilo haberent: adductus sum artes liberales sic conscribere, ut ex iis Methodum Rami: praecepta vero plerag;[?] Domini Melanchthonis studiosi adolescentes percipere⌣ possent. Nam ut verum asseram, praecepta D. Philippi Melanchthonis nullo modo a studiosa sunt juventute floccifacienda: pia enim illa Melanchthonis anima; ita quoq; liberales artes, licet non Methodo usque quaque succin-

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment ("thodi,", the end of "Methodi") and is kept as a fragment. The small cup-shaped marks (⌣) after "Aristotelis", "corruscatione" and "percipere" are printed signs, probably references or quantity marks, and are copied as they appear; their meaning is not clear from the scan. "plerag;" is an abbreviation (plerasque) whose last letters are doubtful. The page is set in roman with italics. The paragraph runs on from the previous page and ends mid-word at "succin-", which continues on the next page.
